policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV main text reads 'David said to Solomon his son' — 'his son' renders the ketiv בנו (3ms suffix), not the qere בְּנִי 'my son', which would place 'My son' inside the quoted speech. The ASV note 'According to another reading, My son, as for me etc.' confirms the qere is the reading the ASV did not follow; the decision rests on the main-text wording.
